object_context: Whole-space Type-I Navier-Stokes blow-up-classification child for Clay statement (A). Test whether an exact scale-critical vorticity-direction/geometric-depletion property is inherited from the already registered Albritton-Barker finite-I ancient class strongly enough to activate a source-matched regularity or rigidity theorem. This is an inheritance/interface audit, not a new regularity theorem; Type-II remains out of scope.
structural_coordinates: unforced whole-space 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes; viscosity normalized to 1
parabolic scaling u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), p_lambda=lambda^2 p(lambda x,lambda^2 t), omega_lambda=lambda^2 omega(lambda x,lambda^2 t)
vorticity direction xi=omega/|omega| is dimensionless where omega is nonzero, but spatial C^alpha seminorms scale like lambda^alpha and xi is undefined at vorticity zeros

Albritton-Barker finite I is local scale-invariant velocity/pressure/gradient control and yields a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution in the Type-I class; it is not itself a vorticity-direction modulus

registered compactness gives strong local L3 convergence of velocity and weak local L3/2 pressure convergence; the local energy component also supplies only weak derivative compactness at the natural level
strong L3_loc velocity convergence plus bounded local gradient energy does not continuously transfer normalized curl direction because curl costs one derivative and normalization is unstable at zeros
taking curl removes pressure from the evolution equation, but nonlocality remains through the Biot-Savart/strain singular-integral relation entering vortex stretching

geometric criteria in the literature impose additional conditions on vorticity direction, projected vorticity, or high-vorticity superlevel geometry; the active question is inheritance of such a condition, not whether those conditional criteria are valid

Barker-Prange Type-I alignment is a half-space/no-slip and ODE-Type-I theorem; its geometry hypothesis is separately assumed and its domain/Type-I notion cannot be silently identified with the whole-space finite-I class
recent logarithmic-depletion work is treated as a primary preprint search analogue only; its extra concentration and direction-space assumptions cannot bear theorem authority in this cycle
Type-II singularities require a separate normalization/classification mechanism and are not addressed by finite-I inheritance

target_interface.input: a relevant finite-I Type-I blow-up sequence/ancient limit in the registered whole-space class
target_interface.desired_output: a uniform scale-critical vorticity-direction or geometric-depletion certificate G that survives the blow-up limit and exactly matches a primary-source regularity/Liouville theorem
target_interface.audit_question: Do the currently registered finite-I estimates and compactness topology themselves control any such G without adding an unproved derivative/normalization assumption?

solved_analogues.fact: whole-space geometric regularity via control of vorticity direction; conditional criterion, not an inheritance theorem
regularity from scale-critical L4_t L2_x control of vorticity projected onto a varying plane, with bounded gradient of the plane normal

solved_analogues.source: Tobias Barker and Christophe Prange, arXiv:1906.08225
solved_analogues.fact: half-space/no-slip ODE-Type-I regularity when vorticity direction is uniformly continuous on high-vorticity subsets of shrinking parabolic regions

near_solved_analogues.source: Dallas Albritton and Tobias Barker, arXiv:1811.00502
near_solved_analogues.fact: local Type-I singularities correspond to nontrivial mild bounded ancient solutions with the registered Type-I condition; local compactness does not state vorticity-direction inheritance

July 2026 preprint proposes singularity evasion under weak-L3/2 vorticity concentration plus logarithmically weighted local BMO control of vorticity direction; retained only as proposal/shadow search analogue

required_assumptions: uniform geometric control on xi on the source theorem's high-vorticity set
target_disanalogies: finite I controls velocity/pressure/local gradient budgets rather than a modulus of normalized vorticity
weak derivative compactness does not preserve angles of curl

required_assumptions: uniform continuity of vorticity direction on specified high-vorticity subsets
target_disanalogies: active Type-I quantity is Albritton-Barker finite I, not merely the ODE rate
alignment is an extra hypothesis in the source theorem

required_assumptions: bounded spatial gradient of the varying plane normal
target_disanalogies: no preferred plane field or its gradient is supplied by finite I
deriving the plane field from xi reintroduces normalized-vorticity regularity

counterexample_first_calibration.model: On a fixed local periodic box, w_n(x)=(0,n^{-1} sin(n x_1),0) is divergence free, w_n->0 strongly in L3, and ||grad w_n||_L2 stays O(1), while curl w_n=(0,0,cos(n x_1)) has rapidly flipping normalized direction away from its zeros.
counterexample_first_calibration.scope: functional-analytic topology calibration only; not asserted to solve Navier-Stokes and not a PDE counterexample
counterexample_first_calibration.purpose: falsify any purely topological inference from strong local velocity convergence plus natural weak gradient control to a uniform modulus of vorticity direction
